description: Posit Connect client contract shared by pkg-r and pkg-py. The source is tests/shared/connect.json; the copy under pkg-r/tests/testthat/fixtures/shared/ is generated by scripts/sync-shared.sh. Edit the source and re-run that script.

environment.description: Environment variables the client reads. A publisher or Connect itself sets these, so both packages must read the same names.

server_normalization.description: Server URLs a publisher might configure, and the base each reduces to. Publishers paste whatever the dashboard shows them, so a form one package accepts and the other does not sends requests to the wrong place.

cases.name: an already normalized url is unchanged
a trailing slash is dropped
repeated trailing slashes are dropped
the api root is dropped
the api root with a trailing slash is dropped
a doubled slash before the api root is dropped
a server hosted under a path keeps the path

runtime_detection.description: Whether the process is running as content on Connect. Connect sets POSIT_PRODUCT, and some processes carry only the content guid. `env` maps a variable to its value, or to null when it is unset.

cases.name: a local session is not Connect
the product variable identifies Connect
another Posit product is not Connect
a content guid alone identifies Connect
an empty content guid is not Connect

api_request.description: Where a request lands, given the normalized server and the path segments the caller passes. Both packages address Connect's versioned API root.

cases.name: a content item
a content item's permissions
the users collection

collaborator_grant.description: The permission commons creates so a user can read this content's trajectories. Reading traces needs editor-level access, and Connect's permissions API spells that role "owner"; it rejects "editor". A lesser permission on the content, such as the viewer role someone gets when the app is shared with them, does not carry trace access, so it is not a reason to skip them.

sharing.description: Who gets a grant, given the usernames asked for and the permissions that already exist on the content. `expected` lists the principals granted, in order. Test doubles resolve username `x` to principal `guid-x`.

cases.name: a user with no permission is granted one
a user who already holds the role is left alone
a user with only viewer access is still granted the role
only the user missing the role is granted
a username is matched regardless of case
case variants of one username are granted once
